primaryVerses.text: The king and his men went to Jerusalem against the Jebusites, the inhabitants of the land, who spoke to David, saying, “The blind and the lame will keep you out of here,” thinking, “David can’t come in here.”
primaryVerses.finding: Jebusites is explicitly plural and described as inhabitants of Jerusalem; supports collective knownBy/base summary.

primaryVerses.text: Nevertheless David took the stronghold of Zion. This is David’s city.
primaryVerses.finding: The WEB says David took Zion stronghold. It does not name Jebusites; valid display gate for the linked article introduction, which says conquest was completed by David.

primaryVerses.text: David said on that day, “Whoever strikes the Jebusites, let him go up to the watercourse and strike those lame and blind, who are hated by David’s soul.” Therefore they say, “The blind and the lame can’t come into the house.”
primaryVerses.finding: Jebusites explicitly plural; fact is correctly gated at this verse.

primaryVerses.text: When the angel stretched out his hand toward Jerusalem to destroy it, the LORD relented of the disaster, and said to the angel who destroyed the people, “It is enough. Now withdraw your hand.” The LORD’s angel was by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.
primaryVerses.finding: “the Jebusite” is an individual epithet for Araunah, not a collective-use occurrence.

primaryVerses.text: Gad came that day to David and said to him, “Go up, build an altar to the LORD on the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.”
primaryVerses.finding: “the Jebusite” again describes Araunah individually; it does not belong in the collective passages.

wikipedia.title: Jebusites
wikipedia.support: The page describes Jebusites as a Canaanite tribe inhabiting Jerusalem and explicitly ties the account to Samuel; the same introduction says David completed the conquest, so profile/article link is gated at 2SA5:7. This supports the group connection, not the genealogical ancestor ID in Genesis.
